sentences.text:
THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT 1.
The claimant, being dissatisfied with the compensation of Rs.89,500/- awarded by the Tribunal, is in appeal.

2. The Tribunal had exonerated the liability to pay compensation on the owner of the offending vehicle on the ground that the driver of offending vehicle was holding only a light motor vehicle licence and hence he was not permitted to drive goods vehicle.

3. In the light of the decision reported in the case of Mukund Dewangan Vs. Oriental Insurance Co.
Ltd - (2017)14 SCC 663 , the finding of the Tribunal exonerating liability cannot be sustained and secondly it is held that the insurer would be held liable to pay the compensation for the injuries suffered by the claimant.

entities.text:
Mukund Dewangan Vs. Oriental Insurance Co.
Ltd - (2017)14 SCC 663
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 4. In my view, for the injuries suffered by the claimant the Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.89,500/-.
Having regard to the fact that the claimant had suffered minor fractures, the award of Rs.89,500/- is just and proper and does not require any enhancement.
5. Consequently, the appeal is allowed only to the extent of fastening of liability on the insurer and the award of compensation is however, confirmed.
6. The appeal is accordingly allowed in part.
